question: Excuse me, I have a question: how long did you brainstorm and plan the concept before posting this novel? I'm thinking of creating a novel myself, so could you tell me as a reference?
answer:
At first, all I came up with was the premise: 'A protagonist summoned to another world with only the ability to Return by Death works desperately while looping to make the king-candidate heroine the ruler.'
I talked to a friend about it, chatted for half a day at a family restaurant to form a rough storyline, then went home, started writing, and began posting about three days later—that was the flow.
To make it an interesting work, I'm constantly refining the concept, but it's like fleshing out the skeleton as I write. If we talk purely about the initial conception period, it would be... half a day, so considering fine-tuning details, it was probably about a week.
That said, I've been writing novels for 10 years, so once I start, I believe I have the ability to structure a story reasonably well.
If you're starting to write a novel, rather than a massive epic, aim for a medium-length story about the size of a single paperback volume. If you complete several stories until the end and build up writing skill and creativity, you can write anything on pure momentum after that.
I look forward to the day I can read LENEY-sama's work.
Even when you start writing, don't stop reading this story, okay!
